text:
St. Louis arrives at Newark on the second night of a quick turnaround, game three of a four-game road trip (1-1-0 so far), after a 3-1 loss at the Rangers, who snapped a four-game winless run against them. The Blues are 2-3-0 in their last five and without Dillon Dube. New Jersey beat Edmonton 4-3 in a shootout on Tuesday, ending the Oilers' three-game winning streak, and are 4-1-0 in their last five. Our numbers say the Devils are better than their record: a +8 goal difference on +15.3 expected, with goaltending costing them.

The chance battle favors New Jersey. At five on five the Devils have taken 58% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) against 50% for St. Louis, and their power play (0.78 expected goals per game) tops the Blues' (0.51). Our model projects 3.41 goals for NJD and 2.69 for STL. In net, projected starters Connor Hellebuyck (-0.5 goals saved above expected, meaning goals stopped beyond what the shots warranted) and Jordan Binnington (-5.1) both have rough starts, though Binnington's gap is wider. He is in over Joel Hofer, who has 11 of the Blues' 15 starts.

Jack Hughes is our top scorer pick at 42%, and Nico Hischier is two points from 500 for his career. Arseny Gritsyuk, drafted 129th overall, has 10 points in his last ten and is earning them. Our under-the-radar pick is Luke Evangelista, 58% for a point, because his line creates chances. For St. Louis, Mason McTavish is pointless in five straight despite 3.4 expected goals, so the chances are there.
